title: Teacup cover and stand, silver, chased and gilt, made in the workshop of Khem Raj Sakya, Patan, Nepal, 1982
medium: Silver, embossed, chased and gilt; with porcelain
provenance: Silver stand made in the workshop of Khem Raj Sakya, Patan, Nepal, 1982, fitted with a Chinese porcelain cup, c. 1700-1800. From the workshop of the Newar, Khem Raj Sakya in Patan, the piece illustrates the continuing patronage of the Newari craftsman by the Tibetan community in exile within Nepal. An ex-trader to Lhasa, Khem Raj turned to metal-working on his return from Tibet in 1962. He learnt his craft from Hira Ratra Shakya (whose father was in Tibet, Lhasa and Shitgatse 1936-39) and brother. He employs seven in his Patan workshop.

title: Nepal; town life in the Khumbu, 1986. Namche Bazar (altitude 3446 metres), a bustling and prosperous market town, is the largest Sherpa settlement in the Khumbu. Most have windows and doors at the front of the building only, the back being built into the side of the mountain. Said to have been collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey (see Acq biography) during his military service in wartime India, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station, on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.

Said to have been collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey (see Acq biography) during his military service in wartime India, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station, on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.

Said to have been collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey (see Acq biography) during his military service in wartime India, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station, on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.

Said to have been collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey (see Acq biography) during his military service in wartime India, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station, on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.
